title: Friends from different cultures: what we share
examples: How can I be friends with someone from a different culture?
How do I ask about someone's culture without being rude?
What do people from different cultures have in common?

explain.say: Here is a puzzle: two friends can eat different food, speak different languages at home and celebrate different festivals, and still laugh at exactly the same jokes. Look at the board. Some things can be different.

draw.text: Friends from different cultures: what we share

explain.say: Food at home, festivals, languages, clothes, and prayers or beliefs can all be different. Culture means the way of life a group of people share. What is one thing from your culture you love?
Now look at the other group: love for family, liking jokes, feeling sad sometimes, wanting friends and loving games. These are often the same everywhere. Can you see how much we share?
Meet Fatima and Lena. Fatima has biryani, and Lena has a cheese sandwich. Lena is curious, not rude: what is that? It smells great! Asking kindly is how you learn about a culture.

faq.q: How can I ask about someone's culture kindly?
faq.a: Be curious and friendly: That looks yummy, what is it? or: What do you do for your festival? Listen and avoid words like weird or gross.
asks: How do I ask about someone's culture without being rude?

faq.a: Culture is the way of life a group of people share: their food, languages, festivals, clothes, music, beliefs and customs.
asks: Tell me about the Can be different

faq.q: What do people from different cultures have in common?
faq.a: Lots! Most people love their families, like to laugh, want friends, feel sad sometimes and enjoy games and good food.
asks: Tell me about the Often the same

faq.q: What if someone's food or clothes seem strange to me?
faq.a: They might seem new to you, and yours might seem new to them. Saying it is new to me, can you tell me about it? is kinder than calling it strange.
asks: Is it rude to say food is weird?

faq.q: Can I join a friend's festival?
faq.a: Often yes, if you are invited. Ask your friend what to wear or bring, and enjoy learning something new.
asks: Can I celebrate Eid or Diwali with my friend?

facts: The International Organization for Migration reports about 281 million people lived outside their country of birth in 2020.
The United Nations marks the World Day for Cultural Diversity on 21 May.

quiz.say: Your friend brings a lunch you have never seen. What is a kind thing to say?
quiz.why: A curious, friendly question shows respect.

quiz.say: Which is something people from different cultures often share?
quiz.why: Loving family is common across cultures.
